gloss: take possession, inherit; dispossess, drive out
summary: To come into possession of what was another's: to take a land and live in it in place of those who held it, and to succeed a man as his heir. Its object is often the people dispossessed as well as their land, so the qal both possesses and dispossesses, and the hiphil drives out the nations or makes another possess. Its great theme is the land Yahweh swore to Abraham “to possess it”, which the meek, the righteous and those who wait on Yahweh will inherit for ever (Psa 37:11, 29), a promise Jesus repeats (Mat 5:5). Arabic wariṯa, Ugaritic yrṯ and Aramaic and Syriac yrt “inherit” show the same root, with ṯ behind the ש.

words.gloss: take possession, possess; dispossess; be heir, inherit; (hiphil) drive out, cause to possess
words.summary: About 230 times, above all in Deuteronomy and Joshua. To possess is to take another's place: “the sons of Esau dispossessed them … and dwelt in their place” (Deu 2:12). So the same verb takes the land as object (possess it) or its people (dispossess them), and the heir is the one who takes a dead man's place. The qal tokens of רָשׁ “poor” (1Sa 18:23; Pro 14:20 and others) are filed under this key by spelling; they are the participle of רוּשׁ “be poor” and are not cited here.

stems.gloss: take possession, possess; dispossess; be heir, inherit

senses.definition: To go in and take a land, a city or a property and hold it as one's own, usually from those who held it before, and dwell in it.

evidence.note: “Go in and possess (וּרְשׁוּ) the land which Yahweh swore to your fathers … to give to them and to their seed after them.”
“Yahweh gave to Israel all the land that he swore to give to their fathers, וַיִּרָשׁוּהָ and they dwelt in it”: given, then taken and lived in.
“Not by their sword did they possess the land … but your right hand.”
“To give you this land לְרִשְׁתָּהּ, to possess it.”
“Go up and possess the land that I have given you”, and they rebelled.
“The sons went in and possessed the land, and you subdued before them the dwellers of the land.”
“The land which your fathers possessed, and you will possess it.”
The settlers brought by the king of Assyria “possessed Samaria and dwelt in its cities”, in place of Israel.
Naphtali: “possess the west and the south.”
Jezebel: “Arise, רֵשׁ the vineyard of Naboth … for Naboth is not alive.”
“Have you murdered and also taken possession?”
The Chaldeans go through the earth “to seize dwellings not his own”.
“Let us possess for ourselves the pastures of God.”
Edom: “the two nations and the two lands shall be mine, and we will possess it”, though Yahweh was there.
The worst of the nations “will possess their houses”.
Of Edom laid waste: the pelican and the owl “will possess it”.
“Nettles will possess the precious things of their silver.”

senses.definition: With a people as object: to take their land from them and live in their place.

evidence.note: “The sons of Esau יִירָשׁוּם, and destroyed them from before them, and dwelt in their place.”
“Yahweh destroyed them before them, וַיִּירָשֻׁם and dwelt in their place.”
“You are crossing the Jordan today to go in to dispossess nations greater and mightier than you.”
“Israel will dispossess those who dispossessed him (אֶת־יֹרְשָׁיו).”
“Why has their king dispossessed Gad, and his people dwelt in his cities?”
“These nations whom you are dispossessing listen to soothsayers.”
“Your seed will dispossess nations and make desolate cities inhabited.”
“That they may possess the remnant of Edom and all the nations over whom my name is called.”
“The Negev will possess the mountain of Esau, and the Shephelah the Philistines.”
“Have you invited us here to dispossess us?”
One of the things the earth cannot bear: “a maidservant when she dispossesses her mistress”, takes her place.
“I will yet bring the possessor (הַיֹּרֵשׁ) upon you, dweller of Mareshah”, a play on the town's name.

senses.gloss: be heir, inherit (a man or his property)
senses.definition: To succeed a man and receive what was his at his death; the participle יוֹרֵשׁ is the heir.

evidence.note: Abram: “You have given me no seed, and behold, a son of my house יוֹרֵשׁ אֹתִי, is my heir.”
“This one will not be your heir, but one who comes from your own bowels, he will be your heir.”
“The son of this slave woman shall not inherit with my son, with Isaac”; quoted in Gal 4:30.
The Peshitta has the same root: לָא נִארַתֿ, “will not inherit”.
“Let us destroy the heir also”, and quench the coal that is left, leaving no name or remnant.
“Has Israel no sons? Has he no heir?”
The inheritance goes to the nearest kinsman, “and he shall possess it”.
“Every daughter possessing an inheritance … so that the sons of Israel may possess each the inheritance of his fathers.”

senses.definition: Of Abraham's seed and of the righteous: to receive the land Yahweh swore to the fathers, and hold it for ever, when the wicked are cut off.

evidence.note: “The meek will inherit the land (יִירְשׁוּ־אָרֶץ) and delight themselves in abundance of peace”; quoted by Jesus in Mat 5:5.
“The righteous will inherit the land and dwell upon it for ever (לָעַד).”
“Evildoers will be cut off, but those who wait on Yahweh, they will inherit the land.”
“Wait on Yahweh and keep his way, and he will raise you up to inherit the land; when the wicked are cut off, you will see it.”
“Blessed are the meek, for they will inherit the earth”; the Peshitta's נִארתֻֿונ לַארעָא is the same root.
“The blessing of Abraham … to inherit the land of your sojournings, which God gave to Abraham.”
“Your seed will possess the gate of his enemies.”
“The one who takes refuge in me will inherit (יִנְחַל) the land and possess (יִירַשׁ) my holy mountain.”
“Your people, all of them righteous, will possess the land for ever.”
“From Judah one who possesses my mountains; my chosen ones will possess it.”
“His seed will inherit the land.”
“God will save Zion and build the cities of Judah, and they will dwell there and possess it.”
“On Mount Zion … the house of Jacob will possess their possessions.”
“I will bring them back to the land that I gave to their fathers, and they will possess it.”
“Righteousness, righteousness you shall pursue, that you may live and possess the land.”

senses.definition: To lose one's goods and livelihood: the passive of dispossession, said of famine, sloth and gluttony.

evidence.note: Joseph: “I will provide for you there … lest you be dispossessed (תִּוָּרֵשׁ), you and your household and all that is yours.”
“Do not love sleep lest you come to poverty; open your eyes, be satisfied with bread.”
“The drunkard and the glutton will come to poverty, and slumber will clothe with rags.”
“Lest I be dispossessed and steal”, set against “lest I be full and deny”.

senses.definition: Of the cricket that takes over trees and crops.

evidence.note: “All your trees and the fruit of your ground the cricket יְיָרֵשׁ, will take possession of.”

stems.gloss: drive out, dispossess; cause to possess, give as a possession; take possession; make poor

senses.definition: To remove a people from their land so that another may hold it; above all of Yahweh driving out the nations before Israel, and of Israel failing to drive them out.

evidence.note: “You shall drive out all the dwellers of the land from before you, and destroy all their carved figures.”
“If you do not drive out the dwellers of the land, those you leave will be splinters in your eyes and thorns in your sides.”
“For the wickedness of these nations Yahweh is driving them out (מוֹרִישָׁם) from before you.”
“The Asherite dwelt among the Canaanite … for he did not drive him out.”
Judah “possessed the hill country, but could not drive out the dwellers of the valley, for they had chariots of iron”.
“I also will no more drive out before them any of the nations that Joshua left.”
“I myself will drive them out before the sons of Israel.”
“I will drive out nations before you and enlarge your border.”
“You with your hand drove out the nations, but them you planted.”
“Did you not drive out the dwellers of this land before your people Israel, and give it to the seed of Abraham your friend for ever?”
The enemy at the sea: “my hand will dispossess them”.
Of Israel itself: “I will strike them with pestilence and dispossess them, and make of you a nation greater than they.”
Of Tyre: “Behold, the Lord will dispossess her.”
“He swallows wealth and vomits it; God drives it out of his belly.”

senses.gloss: cause to possess, give as a possession, leave as an inheritance
senses.definition: To make another the possessor of land or property, or leave it to one's sons.

evidence.note: “What Chemosh your god causes you to possess (יוֹרִישְׁךָ), will you not possess it?”
“To drive us out of your possession which you caused us to possess (הוֹרַשְׁתָּנוּ).”
“That you may … eat the good of the land and leave it as an inheritance to your sons for ever.”
“You make me inherit the iniquities of my youth.”

senses.definition: As the qal: to seize and hold a city or land.

evidence.note: “Rise from the ambush and take possession of the city, and Yahweh your God will give it into your hand.”
“You shall possess the land and dwell in it, for to you I have given the land to possess it.”
“My servant Caleb … his seed will possess it.”
“The sons of Manasseh could not take possession of these cities.”

senses.definition: To take away a man's goods; the opposite of making rich.

evidence.note: “Yahweh makes poor (מוֹרִישׁ) and makes rich (מַעֲשִׁיר), brings low and lifts up.”

evidence.locator: Gen.15.3, 4; 21.10; Psa.25.13; 37.9, 11; Isa.60.21 → κληρονομέω; κληρονομέω renders יָרַשׁ ×68

evidence.note: “The meek will inherit (κληρονομήσουσιν) the earth”, from Psa 37:11.
Gen 21:10 quoted: the son of the slave woman will not inherit.
“Inherit the kingdom prepared for you from the foundation of the world.”
“Flesh and blood cannot inherit the kingdom of God.”
“The one who overcomes will inherit these things.”
“This is the heir; come, let us kill him and have his inheritance.”
The promise to Abraham and his seed “that he should be heir of the world”.
“If you are Christ's, then you are Abraham's seed, heirs according to the promise.”

evidence.locator: Deu.9.4 מוֹרִישָׁם → ἐξολεθρεύσει; ἐξολοθρεύω renders יָרַשׁ ×16, mostly the hiphil

evidence.note: The New Testament's one use, in the quotation of Deu 18:19, where the Hebrew is another word: the bridge from יָרַשׁ is only the Septuagint's.

parallels.note: “Dwell”: to possess a land is to live in it in another's place.
“Dwell, settle”: the righteous possess the land and dwell on it for ever.
“Receive as an inheritance”: the share given; set beside יָרַשׁ, the taking of it.
“Destroy”: the dispossession of the former peoples.

opposites.note: “Be cut off”: the wicked are cut off, and the meek and righteous inherit the land.

phrases.gloss: go in and possess the land

evidence.note: With עֲלוּ, “go up”.

phrases.gloss: your seed will possess the gate of his enemies

evidence.note: “… the gate of those who hate him.”

words.summary: The juice of the grape, fresh from the press, named with grain and oil as the produce of the land. Ugaritic trṯ and Phoenician trš “wine” are the same word, with the same ṯ; how it comes from the root “take possession” is not clear, and the proposals (the juice “driven out” of the grapes) rest on no evidence.

senses.definition: The wine of the year's vintage, the second of the land's three staples, given by Yahweh as blessing and withheld in judgment; its firstfruits and tithe were brought to the priests and Levites.

evidence.note: “He will bless … your grain and your new wine and your oil.”
“She did not know that I gave her the grain and the new wine and the oil.”
Drought called upon “the grain and the new wine and the oil”.
Isaac's blessing: “abundance of grain and new wine”.
“All the best of the oil and all the best of the new wine and grain, their firstfruits”, given to the priests.
“You have put gladness in my heart more than when their grain and new wine abound.”

senses.definition: The juice in the cluster and in the vat, before it is the wine that is drunk.

evidence.note: “As the new wine is found in the cluster, and one says, Do not destroy it, for a blessing is in it.”
“You will tread … new wine (תִּירוֹשׁ), but not drink wine (יַיִן)”: the juice trodden, the wine that would have been drunk.
“Your vats will burst with new wine.”

senses.gloss: new wine that takes the heart
senses.definition: With wine, a drink that can overpower the understanding.

evidence.note: “Whoredom and wine and new wine take away the heart.”
The vine: “Shall I leave my new wine, which cheers God and men?”

evidence.locator: Hos.2.10 תִּירוֹשׁ → οἶνος; οἶνος renders תִּירוֹשׁ ×29

evidence.note: “Do not harm the oil and the wine”: the staples named together, as in Deu 7:13.

parallels.note: “Grain”, with יִצְהָר “fresh oil”: the three staples of the land.

phrases.gloss: grain and new wine and oil

words.summary: A net spread to catch birds or beasts, and in figure the plots of the wicked and the judgment of God; also the bronze grating of the altar. Ugaritic rṯt “net” is the same word with the same ṯ. The net that takes and holds its prey may be what ties it to “take possession”, but the verses do not show it.

senses.definition: A net spread (פָּרַשׂ) or hidden (טָמַן) to catch the feet; of the wicked plotting against the righteous, who are caught in their own net, and of Yahweh's net cast over the rebel.

evidence.note: “You have been a snare (פַּח) at Mizpah and a net spread on Tabor.”
“In vain is the net spread in the eyes of any bird.”
“In the net which they hid their own foot is caught.”
“The proud have hidden a snare for me, and cords; they have spread a net.”
“Without cause they hid for me their net, a pit.”
“He will bring my feet out of the net.”
“A man who flatters his neighbour spreads a net for his steps.”
Of Zedekiah: “I will spread my net over him and he will be caught in my snare, and I will bring him to Babylon … yet he will not see it.”
“He has spread a net for my feet; he has turned me back.”

senses.definition: The bronze lattice-work of the altar of burnt offering, set beneath its ledge.

evidence.note: “A grating, a work of net (מַעֲשֵׂה רֶשֶׁת) of bronze.”

evidence.locator: Psa.9.16 → παγίδι; Psa.25.15 → παγίς; Psa.140.6 → παγίδας; παγίς renders רֶשֶׁת ×7

evidence.note: “Those who will to be rich fall into temptation and a snare.”
The New Testament's word for the fishermen's nets.

parallels.note: “Pit”, dug as the net is hidden.

senses.definition: The land a people or a man holds as theirs, given by Yahweh or come down in the family; and the right to it.

evidence.note: “I will not give you of their land so much as the treading of the sole of a foot, for I have given Mount Seir to Esau as a possession.”
Stephen takes up Deu 2:5's words of Abraham: God “gave him no inheritance in it, not even the treading of a foot”, but promised it to him and his seed; the Peshitta has יָרתֻּותָֿא, the same root.
“The land of his possession which Yahweh gave them.”
“Then you shall return each to his possession which I have given you.”
“A possession for the survivors of Benjamin, that a tribe be not blotted out from Israel.”
“Buy my field … for yours is the right of possession (מִשְׁפַּט הַיְרֻשָּׁה) and yours the redemption.”
“You have given the inheritance of those who fear your name.”
“Your possession which you caused us to possess.”

evidence.locator: κληρονομία renders יְרֻשָּׁה ×6; Deu.2.5, 9, 19 have κλῆρος

evidence.note: “He gave him no inheritance (κληρονομίαν) in it, not even a foot's length”, after Deu 2:5.
“If the inheritance is of the law, it is no longer of promise; but God gave it to Abraham by promise.”

senses.definition: What is given or taken to be held as one's own: the land promised to the fathers, the law given to Jacob, and the land the nations claimed for themselves.

evidence.note: “I will bring you to the land which I raised my hand to give to Abraham, to Isaac and to Jacob, and I will give it to you as a possession.”
“Moses commanded us a law, a possession of the assembly of Jacob.”
The dwellers of Jerusalem of the exiles: “Be far from Yahweh; to us the land is given as a possession.”
“Abraham was one, and he possessed the land; we are many; the land is given to us as a possession”: the claim Yahweh answers in vv. 25–26.
The enemy: “The ancient high places have become our possession.”

evidence.locator: Ezk.36.2 → κατάσχεσιν; κατάσχεσις renders מוֹרָשָׁה ×4, κληρονομία ×4 (Deu.33.4)

evidence.note: God “promised to give it to him for a possession (εἰς κατάσχεσιν)”, the words of Exo 6:8 and Ezk 33:24.
The tabernacle brought in with Joshua “into the possession of the nations whom God drove out”.

senses.definition: What one holds as one's own; in Job, the things of the heart held most dear.

evidence.note: “The house of Jacob will possess their possessions.”
Of Babylon: “I will make it a possession of the hedgehog, and pools of water.”
“My days are past, my plans are broken off, the possessions of my heart”: what the heart held.

senses.definition: A land taken by another and held by him.

evidence.note: Balaam: “Edom will be a possession, and Seir a possession, of his enemies, while Israel does valiantly.”

words.summary: The Peshitta's verb for κληρονομέω: to inherit, and to come into the land, the kingdom, eternal life or the blessing. It is the verb of Mat 5:5, where Jesus repeats Psa 37:11.

senses.definition: To come into what is promised as an heir does: the earth, the kingdom of God, eternal life, the blessing.

evidence.note: “Blessed are the meek, for they נִארתֻֿונ לַארעָא, will inherit the earth.”
“Come, blessed of my Father, יִרַתֿו the kingdom prepared for you from the foundation of the world.”
“Flesh and blood cannot inherit (לְמִארַתֿ) the kingdom of heaven, nor does corruption inherit incorruption.”
From Gen 21:10: “the son of the bondwoman will not inherit with the son of the free woman”.
“… and will inherit eternal life.”
The name the Son “inherited”, more excellent than the angels'.
Esau “wished to inherit the blessing, and was rejected”.
Wives “inherit with you the gift of eternal life”.
“The one who overcomes will inherit these things, and I will be his God.”

senses.definition: The one who receives a father's estate; the Son, heir of all things, and those who are his, heirs of the promise to Abraham.

evidence.note: The husbandmen: “This is the heir (יָרתָּא); come, let us kill him and seize his inheritance.”
“As long as the heir is a child, he differs nothing from a servant, though he is lord of all.”
The Son, “whom he appointed heir of all things”.
The promise to Abraham and his seed, “that he should be heir of the world”.
“If sons, also heirs: heirs of God, and sharers in the inheritance of Jesus the Messiah.”
“If you are the Messiah's, you are Abraham's seed, and heirs by the promise.”
The poor of the world, chosen “to be heirs in the kingdom which God promised to those who love him”.

senses.definition: What comes to an heir: a family's estate, the land promised to Abraham, and the inheritance of the holy ones in the kingdom.

evidence.note: “Teacher, tell my brother to divide the inheritance with me.”
“He gave him no inheritance in it, not even a footstep; but promised to give it to him and to his seed … to possess it.”
Abraham went out “to the place which he was to receive for an inheritance”.
He sojourned in the land of promise with Isaac and Jacob, “heirs (בּנַי יָרתֻּותָֿא) of the promise”.
“The promise of the eternal inheritance.”
“An inheritance incorruptible and undefiled and unfading, reserved in heaven for you.”

senses.definition: Land given as a possession; and the inheritance among the holy ones.

evidence.note: “He destroyed seven nations in the land of Canaan and gave them their land as a possession.”
“Into the land which God gave them as a possession from the nations whom he drove out.”
“To give you an inheritance among all the holy ones.”

evidence.locator: Book I, p. 2934, art. ورث, وَرِثَ (n41827)
evidence.note: “He inherited … وَرِثَ أَبَاهُ He inherited [the property of] his father.”

evidence.locator: Book I, p. 2934, art. ورث, form 4 (n41829)
evidence.note: “He (his father) made him to inherit the thing.”

evidence.note: The Targums use it in the very verses where the Hebrew has יָרַשׁ.

cognates.note: Phoenician š answers both š and ṯ.

doctrine.statement: Psalm 37 sets two ends side by side five times: “evildoers will be cut off, but those who wait on Yahweh, they will inherit the land” (v. 9); “the meek will inherit the land and delight themselves in abundance of peace” (v. 11); “those blessed by him will inherit the land, and those cursed by him will be cut off” (v. 22); “the righteous will inherit the land and dwell upon it for ever” (v. 29); “wait on Yahweh … and he will raise you up to inherit the land; when the wicked are cut off you will see it” (v. 34). The land is one to be dwelt upon, and the dwelling is “for ever”; the wicked are not sent elsewhere but cut off, “yet a little while and the wicked will not be” (v. 10). Isaiah says the same of Zion's people: “all of them righteous, they will possess the land for ever” (Isa 60:21), and “the one who takes refuge in me will inherit the land and possess my holy mountain” (Isa 57:13). Jesus took up verse 11 unchanged, “Blessed are the meek, for they will inherit the earth” (Mat 5:5), and the Peshitta keeps the very root, נִארתֻֿונ לַארעָא. So the reward of the righteous is not a place away from the earth but the earth itself, held for ever, once the wicked have been cut off from it.

Yahweh brought Abram out of Ur “to give you this land to possess it (לְרִשְׁתָּהּ)”, and Abram asked, “How shall I know that I will possess it?” (Gen 15:7–8). Isaac blessed Jacob with “the blessing of Abraham … to possess the land of your sojournings, which God gave to Abraham” (Gen 28:4), and Yahweh swore it “to Abraham, to Isaac and to Jacob, to give to them and to their seed after them” (Deu 1:8). Yet Stephen says God “gave him no inheritance in it, not even a foot's length, but promised to give it to him for a possession, and to his seed after him” (Act 7:5), in the words Deu 2:5 uses of land not given; Hebrews says Abraham went out “to the place he was to receive as an inheritance”, sojourned in it “as in a foreign land … with Isaac and Jacob, heirs with him of the same promise”, and that they “all died in faith, not having received the promises” (Heb 11:8–9, 13). When Israel's later dwellers claimed, “Abraham was one, and he possessed the land”, Yahweh answered that they would not possess it (Ezk 33:24–26). Paul calls the promise to Abraham and his seed the promise “that he should be heir of the world” (Rom 4:13), and the seed is the Messiah and those who are his: “if you are Christ's, you are Abraham's seed, heirs according to the promise” (Gal 3:16, 29). From the verses: the promise was of the land itself, sworn to Abraham personally as well as to his seed; Abraham never held it, and died not having received it; so it is still to be fulfilled, to Abraham and his seed together, which can only be when the dead are raised.

The Son is the heir: “This is the heir; come, let us kill him” (Mat 21:38), “whom he appointed heir of all things” (Heb 1:2); and those who are his are “heirs of God, and joint heirs with Christ” (Rom 8:17). The time of the inheriting is given: “When the Son of man comes in his glory … then the king will say to those at his right hand, Come, blessed of my Father, inherit the kingdom prepared for you” (Mat 25:31, 34). And its condition: “flesh and blood cannot inherit the kingdom of God, nor does corruption inherit incorruption … the dead will be raised incorruptible, and we shall be changed” (1Co 15:50–52). Until then the inheritance is “kept” for them, “ready to be revealed in the last time” (1Pe 1:4–5), and the spirit given now is the pledge of it “until the redemption” (Eph 1:14). From the verses: no one inherits at death; the heirs receive the kingdom together, when Christ returns and they are raised and made incorruptible.

Israel was told plainly why the nations were driven out: “not for your righteousness or the uprightness of your heart do you go in to possess their land, but for the wickedness of these nations Yahweh your God is driving them out before you, and to establish the word he swore to your fathers” (Deu 9:4–5). The same law that gave the land warned that those who corrupted themselves would “perish quickly from the land which you are crossing the Jordan to possess” (Deu 4:26), and Yahweh threatened Israel itself in the wilderness, “I will strike them with pestilence and dispossess them (וְאוֹרִשֶׁנּוּ)” (Num 14:12). When the dwellers among the ruins claimed the land as Abraham's sons, the answer was, “You eat with the blood, you lift your eyes to your idols, and shed blood; and shall you possess the land?” (Ezk 33:25–26). Righteousness is the way to it: “Righteousness, righteousness you shall pursue, that you may live and possess the land” (Deu 16:20). From the verses: the land is Yahweh's gift by oath, not Israel's by merit; the same verb that drove out the nations for wickedness could dispossess Israel, and it is held only by those who walk in his ways.
